credit: Contains bathing water data from the Environmental Protection Agency (Ireland), Bathing Water Open Data API, licensed under CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). SwimSignal reorders the EPA's samples by water and date and draws them; the values are the EPA's, unchanged.

claim.public_wording: Lab samples taken by the official body, each on the date shown. A sample describes the water at that place and time only. SwimSignal makes no forecast here and adds no estimate.
not_claimed: that the water was safe or unsafe on any day other than a sample's, or at any other time that day
a rating: the official rating uses four seasons of scheduled samples by a set method

qualifiers.<: Below the lab's lower limit: fewer than that number were found, possibly none. It is not a count of that number.
qualifiers.>: Above the lab's upper limit: more than that number, how many more is not known.

methods: The EPA's data does not name a lab method for each sample.
Lower limits differ from lab to lab: most give '<10', some '<1', and a few '<5', '<20' or '<50'. A plain count of 1 to 9 can only come from a lab whose limit is lower than 10.

Upper limits also differ: '>2419' and '>24196' are the top of a most-probable-number tray, read neat or diluted ten times (inferred from the values; the EPA does not say), and '>2000', '>2005' or '>2010' come from other labs.
A count of 0 is given as the EPA lists it.
Each sample also has the EPA's own word for it, Excellent, Good, Sufficient or Poor, which the EPA assesses against the standards in the Bathing Water Quality Regulations 2008.
In-season samples run from 22 May to 15 September. Samples outside those dates are voluntary, reported by some councils since 2016, and do not count towards a rating.

Before its December report each year, the EPA keeps only the scheduled in-season samples of that season and drops the investigative ones, so a past season can lose samples between downloads (25,978 results on 31 October 2026, 25,895 on 13 November 2026).
kinds_note: A water's kind is ireland.water_kind's: the EPA's code for designated waters, a check for ten in County Monaghan, else its name. A Lough or Loch with no check has kind 'unknown' and no line.
